refined_question: For some nonnegative integer k, do there exist an integer d with d ≥ 2k + 3 and a finite simple graph G such that G is d-regular and G is a bar k-visibility graph; that is, G admits a representation by pairwise disjoint horizontal bars in the plane in which two vertices are adjacent if and only if there exists a vertical segment joining the corresponding bars that intersects at most k other bars? citeturn7view0turn17search0
justification: The draft is already very close to the paper. The decisive phrase is the threshold d ≥ 2k + 3, which appears verbatim in Open Problem 22 of Section 3.3. The only paper-faithfulness issues are that the draft omits the formal definition of bar k-visibility graph given immediately before the open problems and leaves the integer parameters implicit. To stay as close as possible to the paper, I kept the question existential rather than strengthening it to a universal statement over all k. citeturn7view0turn16search0turn17search0
